title: Microsoft Dataverse: unlicensed Entra users as activity recipients
summary: The administrator enablement path, required roles, recipient licensing exception and roadmap details are supported. The categorical statement about autonomous behaviour goes beyond the documentation, and the security-role prerequisite appears in the checklist but not in the controls table.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: General availability is targeted for January CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists October CY2026 for preview.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The listed release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: Web is the listed platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The listed products include Microsoft 365 app, Dynamics 365 Sales, Dynamics 365 Customer Service and Dataverse.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft 365 app", "Dynamics 365 Sales", "Dynamics 365 Customer Service", "Microsoft Dataverse"]

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-10-19T23:15:15.
Microsoft Learn documents the described behaviour as preview.
claims.quote: Add users without licenses to activity recipient fields (preview)

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; What's changing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Active Entra users in the tenant can be activity recipients without a Dataverse or Power Apps licence.
claims.quote: Turn on this feature in the Power Platform admin center to allow users with a Microsoft Entra ID to be added to activity recipient fields without requiring a Dataverse or Power Apps license.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The unlicensed-user records created by the feature have disabled status.
claims.quote: The user record is created with a disabled status.

claims.where: licensing.notes; What's changing; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Those unlicensed recipients cannot sign in to or run Dynamics 365 apps.
claims.quote: These users can be included as recipients, but they can't sign in to or run Dynamics 365 apps.

claims.claim: The default restriction being relaxed permits only users with a Dataverse or Power Apps licence in activities.
claims.quote: By default, you can only add users with a Dataverse or Power Apps license to activities in Dynamics 365 apps.

claims.claim: The feature requires administrator opt-in.
claims.quote: You need to be a Power Platform administrator to turn on the feature in Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: The feature covers the To, Cc and Bcc fields of email activities.
claims.quote: activity recipient fields, such as the To, Cc, or Bcc fields of an email

claims.claim: The feature covers appointment attendees.
claims.quote: Required Attendees, Optional attendees of appointment

claims.claim: The feature covers Call From and Call To on phone calls.
claims.quote: Call From, or Call To of phone call.

claims.claim: The enabled feature uses the Microsoft Entra ID virtual Dataverse table for user lookup.
claims.quote: After you enable the Activities for users without licenses feature in the Power Platform admin center, the user lookup uses the Microsoft Entra ID table, a virtual Dataverse table

claims.claim: The virtual table displays the current list of active Entra users.
claims.quote: a virtual Dataverse table that displays the current list of active Microsoft Entra ID users.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Selecting an Entra user for an activity creates a corresponding unlicensed-user record in the environment.
claims.quote: When you select a Microsoft Entra ID user for an activity, Dataverse creates a corresponding unlicensed-user record in the environment so that the user can be added to the activity's recipient fields.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Assigning a licence automatically updates the unlicensed user to a licensed user.
claims.quote: When a user without a license is assigned a license, the user is automatically updated to a licensed user and can use the application based on their assigned security roles and permissions.

claims.claim: Earlier activities remain associated with the same user record after licence assignment.
claims.quote: Activities previously associated with the user remain associated with the same user record.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: All users must receive read permission on the Microsoft Entra ID table before the feature is enabled.
claims.quote: Before you turn on the feature in the Power Platform admin center, you need to grant all users in the tenant read permission on the Microsoft Entra ID table.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Entra ID table exposes readable basic directory attributes such as a user's display name.
claims.quote:
DisplayName
Description | The name displayed in the address book for the user.
IsValidForRead | True

claims.claim: Granting the documented table read access requires Privileged Role Administrator.
claims.quote: You need to be a Privileged Role Administrator in the Microsoft Entra admin center to grant users read access to the Microsoft Entra ID table.

claims.claim: Turning on the feature requires Power Platform administrator.
claims.quote: You need to be a Power Platform administrator to turn on the feature in Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: The documented feature switch is configured per environment.
claims.quote:
In the Manage pane, select Environments. Then select an environment.
Select Settings.
Select Product, and then select Features.
Go to Activities for users without licenses.

claims.claim: Existing security roles can be updated to grant read permission on the Entra ID table.
claims.quote: Update each existing security role assigned to users and add read permission for the Microsoft Entra ID table.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; At rollout
claims.claim: A custom security role granting the table read permission can instead be created and assigned to all users.
claims.quote: Create a custom security role that grants read permission for the Microsoft Entra ID table, and then assign the role to all users.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: An overall feature-specific licensing model beyond the recipient exception is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse add unlicensed users activity recipients feature license pricing cost; opened add-unlicensed-users-activities and pricing-billing-skus. Neither states an additional feature-specific licensing model.

claims.claim: No feature-specific charge is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse add unlicensed users activity recipients feature license pricing cost; add-unlicensed-users-activities licensing price billing. Opened feature documentation and pricing-billing-skus; no feature-specific charge found.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The documented implementation work is administrator effort to grant read permission and enable the setting.
claims.quote: Before you turn on the feature in the Power Platform admin center, you need to grant all users in the tenant read permission on the Microsoft Entra ID table.

claims.claim: The cited Power Platform admin center path leads through the environment's Features page to the recipient checkbox.
claims.quote: Select Manage ... select Environments. Then select an environment. ... Select Settings. ... Select Product, and then select Features. ... Activities for users without licenses. ... Select the Add anyone with an Entra ID to an activity's recipients fields checkbox.

claims.claim: No feature-specific API or automation equivalent is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse unlicensed users activity recipients Power Platform API PowerShell enable setting; organization unlicensed activity. Opened feature, pac env and Organization reference; searched Organization for unlicensed/activity-recipient setting names; none found.

claims.claim: No tenant-wide default control for this feature is documented on either UI or automation surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Activities for users without licenses setting API organization tenant; Activities for users without licenses tenant PowerShell. Opened feature and Tenant settings pages; neither documents a tenant-wide default control.

claims.claim: pac env update-settings is documented for updating organization settings generally.
claims.quote: The pac env list-settings command returns all the columns from the first and only row of the organization entity type. Use pac env update-settings to change those settings.

claims.claim: There is no autonomous behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Activities for users without licenses autonomous; opened add-unlicensed-users-activities. It describes record creation upon user selection and automatic updates on licensing, but does not state the categorical absence of autonomous behaviour.
claims.fix: Replace 'No autonomous behaviour.' with 'Dataverse creates a corresponding unlicensed-user record when someone selects a Microsoft Entra ID user for an activity.'

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks administrators to configure is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'update existing roles or create a custom role with read on the Entra ID table' and 'Assign the read role to all users'. Table: only the environment recipient switch and the undocumented tenant-wide default.
claims.fix: The checklist's security-role read-permission configuration has no corresponding controls-table row. Record this coverage gap; do not add a row as part of this correction.

segments: Add anyone with an Entra ID to an activity's recipients fields
